name: B4GALT7
summary: B4GALT7, Friesian dwarfism - a recessive disorder of the Friesian and its crosses. One change in the gene (c.50G>A, p.Arg17Lys), at the last base of exon 1, disrupts splicing of an enzyme needed to build the proteoglycans of cartilage, tendon and growing bone. A horse with two copies is a disproportionate dwarf with lax joints. A carrier is unaffected. UC Davis estimated about 12 percent of Friesians to be carriers.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: B4GALT7 carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy of d. The horse is unaffected, and nothing shows - but half its foals inherit the copy, and two carriers bred together are the only way Friesian dwarfism appears.

phenotypes.name: Friesian dwarfism
phenotypes.description: Disproportionate dwarfism: the limb and rib bones are shortened while the head and the length of the back stay comparatively normal. The fetlocks are lax and over-extend, growth is poor, and the muscles are poorly developed. How severe it is varies from horse to horse.
